transcript: Downtown at New York Theatre Workshop, a woman named Mariam lives in Gaza with her six year old son during wartime. She's training for a situation which for so many of us would be unimaginable — a knock on the roof. This is an initial shot fired at the roof of a targeted building to warn the residents to evacuate shortly before a full scale attack occurs. Throughout this piece, written and performed by Khawla Ibraheem, Mariam runs drills to get a sense of how far she and her son can get from their home within five minutes. What I found so moving about this piece was how juxtaposes our idea of an everyday routine with how a pervasive uncertainty and danger can completely pervert what an everyday routine even looks like. This piece has moments of humor and warmth, but it's overall quite dark and tense with multiple heart stopping moments. I thought this was a really insightful and important piece, although I wish it wasn't necessary. A Knock On The Roof is running through mid-February at New York Theatre Workshop. With that, another program for my collection.
